solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Storage unit, a huge mouthful to say

parts.note: mega is informal for huge or enormous

indicators.note: to say means the word is heard rather than spelt, so a near-twin in sound is entered

parts.note: a bite is a mouthful of food

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a storage unit is an enormous thing to get your mouth around.
explanation.walkthrough: A huge mouthful is a 'mega bite'; spoken aloud it is the computing unit, spelt with a Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A megabyte is a measure of computer memory or disk capacity, roughly a million bytes.

clue.text: Mum's guru gives hands-on treatment

parts.note: Ma is mum, and the apostrophe S is kept as letters
a sage is a wise teacher, like a guru

explanation.surface: A mother's spiritual adviser offers some kind of physical therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A massage is a therapy given by kneading the body with the hands, literally hands-on.

clue.text: Medal I received, retiring

indicators.note: received means the medal word takes in the I, holding it inside

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal or decoration
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone collects a medal as they leave their job.
explanation.walkthrough: A gong is informal British for a medal or honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Going and retiring both mean leaving or departing, as in a retiring or going president.

clue.text: Should this dodgy agency also sell spades?

definitions.text: Should this dodgy agency also sell spades?

parts.note: the real sense: a disreputable business, especially one selling cut-price airline tickets
the joke: buckets go with spades on the beach, so a shop for them might stock both

explanation.walkthrough: A bucket shop is a shady broker or discount travel agent; the clue pretends it is a seaside shop selling buckets, which ought to have spades too.
explanation.definitionFit: Bucket shop is an idiom for an unscrupulous broker or a cut-price ticket seller of doubtful standing.

clue.text: Even risk to cat, being knocked over

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, knocked over means turned upside down, so the cat word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: puss is a familiar word for a cat

explanation.surface: A cat faces some danger as it is bowled over.
explanation.definitionFit: A toss-up is a situation whose outcome is equally likely either way, a fifty-fifty chance.

clue.text: Friends come back for smack

indicators.note: come back means the friends word returns, running right to left

parts.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: Some friends return for a slap on the face, or perhaps for drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: Smack looks like slang for heroin, but here it is a blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a smack, a blow struck with the open hand.

clue.text: A down-to-earth passage

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an aircraft's arrival back on the ground, literally coming down to earth
second meaning: the corridor or level area at the top of a flight of stairs

explanation.walkthrough: Down-to-earth looks like it means sensible; it is meant literally, a plane coming down to the ground, while the area at the top of stairs is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an aircraft touching down and the level area or corridor between flights of stairs.

clue.text: Point out piece of climbing equipment

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone indicates an item of a mountaineer's kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A piton is a metal spike driven into rock as an anchor by mountaineers.

clue.text: In this bag, two things for lawyers to work on

parts.note: the first of two legal matters: a suit is a lawsuit
the second legal matter: a case is a matter argued in court

explanation.surface: Inside this luggage are a pair of briefs for barristers to study.
explanation.walkthrough: Both halves are legal words, a suit and a case, which together make a piece of luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: A suitcase is a rectangular travelling bag for carrying clothes.

clue.text: Small insect somewhat irritating, naturally

indicators.note: somewhat means only some of the following words are used, the run hiding inside them

parts.note: the run straddles the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A tiny bug is, as you would expect, rather annoying.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, often a biting one.

clue.text: Here I may leave empty

parts.note: the place a person drops off something for recycling
read as a noun: an empty is a finished glass container

explanation.walkthrough: Empty reads as an adjective, leaving somewhere vacant; it is a noun, an empty bottle taken to a recycling point.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle bank is a large public container where people deposit used glass for recycling.

clue.text: Fish heading away from seaweed

indicators.note: heading away means the word's head, its first letter, is dropped

parts.note: tangle is a large brown seaweed, a kind of kelp

explanation.surface: A fish swims off away from the weed.
explanation.walkthrough: Tangle is a name for oarweed, a kelp.
explanation.definitionFit: To angle is to fish with a rod and line.

clue.text: I put on a shift with impractical hopes

indicators.note: shift means the letters are moved about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone dons a loose dress, full of unrealistic dreams.
explanation.walkthrough: Shift looks like a garment someone puts on; it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopian describes idealistic schemes for a perfect society that are unlikely ever to be realised.

clue.text: Mischievous and serving own interests? Not at first

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: selfish describes someone serving only their own interests

explanation.surface: Someone is described as naughty and self-centred, though not to begin with.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfish means like an elf, impish and playfully naughty.

clue.text: Feverish winter weeks are annoying

parts.note: February, abbreviated FEB, is a month of winter weeks in the northern hemisphere
rile means irritate, and the plural verb fits weeks

explanation.surface: Someone with a temperature complains that the cold months are tiresome.
explanation.walkthrough: FEB is the calendar abbreviation for February.
explanation.definitionFit: Febrile means relating to fever, or more loosely nervously excited.

clue.text: Part of flower showing black mark

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the tip of a pistil that receives pollen
second meaning: a mark of shame or disgrace

explanation.surface: A gardener sees a dark spot on a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word is the pollen-catching part of a pistil and a lasting sign of social disgrace.

clue.text: Make short work of a card game

parts.note: taken as written
bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: Someone polishes off a hand of cards quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Make short work of usually means do quickly; read literally it is to shorten a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abridge a book or speech is to shorten it while keeping its sense.

clue.text: Laurel's speaking a verse

indicators.note: speaking means the words are heard, not spelt, so a sound-alike is entered

parts.note: Stan Laurel, the comedian, gives 'Stan's'
taken as written

explanation.surface: A poet laureate recites a few lines.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurel is Stan Laurel of Laurel and Hardy; 'Stan's a' said aloud sounds like the poetry term.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: Hair of the dog technician may need

parts.note: lab is short for a Labrador dog
a coat is an animal's covering of hair or fur

explanation.surface: A technician needs a hangover cure, the proverbial hair of the dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair of the dog suggests a morning-after drink; it is read literally as the dog's coat.
explanation.definitionFit: A lab coat is the white protective overall worn by laboratory staff.

clue.text: One used to snare girl with love

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in northern England and Scotland
love is nil in tennis, the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone uses romance to catch a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasso is a rope with a running noose used by cowboys to catch cattle.

clue.text: Composer's frightful glare

definitions.note: read as 'composer is', so the name stands for the whole phrase

indicators.note: frightful suggests something in a terrible mess, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A composer gives a fearsome stare.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Elgar was the English composer of the Enigma Variations.

clue.text: Foreign character turns up in the morning publication

indicators.note: in a down clue, turns up means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning
mag is short for a magazine

explanation.surface: An exotic figure appears in the newspaper one morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma is a letter of the Greek alphabet, so a foreign written character.

clue.text: Dispatch a tiny drink astride horse

indicators.note: astride means the drink straddles the horse, sitting on either side of it

parts.note: a sip is a tiny drink
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Someone sends off a little drink while riding a horse.
explanation.walkthrough: H for horse comes via heroin, both slang names for the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship is to send or dispatch goods.

clue.text: I gave weapons to such a bandit?

parts.note: I is the first person, one
armed means equipped with weapons

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to arming a robber.
explanation.walkthrough: A one-armed bandit is a fruit machine, so-called for its single lever.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-armed bandit is a slot machine, which robs players and has a single arm-like lever.

clue.text: Listen to live between the start of October and the end of January

indicators.note: between means the live word sits inside the two letters on either side
the start of picks the first letter of the month

parts.note: the start of October is its first letter

indicators.note: the end of picks the last letter of the month

parts.note: the end of January is its last letter
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: An instruction to live quietly through the winter months, heeding someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To obey is to heed and do what one is told, as in listening to a parent.

clue.text: This children's contest is in the bag

definitions.text: This children's contest is in the bag

parts.note: a running race at a school sports day
usually meaning certain to be won, but here literal: the runners hop along inside sacks

explanation.walkthrough: In the bag sounds like a sure victory; it is literal, racers standing in sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A sack race is a sports-day event in which competitors jump forward with their legs inside sacks.
